_about: Extra target dates for the Exposure Clock, read on 30 September 2026. The EU roadmap dates are recommendations of the NIS Cooperation Group and set no legal obligation. The NIST dates come from the initial public draft of NIST IR 8547 (12 November 2024); no final version was listed on 30 September 2026, so both stay proposals. Table excerpts give the cell text of one row in reading order.

deadlines.label: EU roadmap: every Member State has taken the First Steps and set up an initial national transition roadmap

provenance.title: A Coordinated Implementation Roadmap for the Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography, Part 1, Version 1.1 (11.06.2025)
provenance.publisher: NIS Cooperation Group work stream on PQC
provenance.excerpt: 1. By 31.12.2026: • At least the First Steps have been implemented by all Member States. • Initial national PQC transition roadmaps have been established by all Member States.
provenance.locator: Section 4.1, Timeline for the transition to PQC, p. 7

provenance.title: A Coordinated Implementation Roadmap for the Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography, Part 1, Version 1.1 (11.06.2025)
provenance.publisher: NIS Cooperation Group work stream on PQC
provenance.excerpt: In particular, it is recommended that all Member States initiate a national PQC transition strategy following First Steps by the end of 2026 and coordinate their efforts at the EU level.

provenance.title: A Coordinated Implementation Roadmap for the Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography
provenance.excerpt: The EU Member States, supported by the Commission, issued a roadmap and timeline to start using a more complex form of cybersecurity, the so-called post-quantum cryptography (PQC).

deadlines.label: EU roadmap: move to post-quantum cryptography completed for high-risk use cases

provenance.title: A Coordinated Implementation Roadmap for the Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography, Part 1, Version 1.1 (11.06.2025)
provenance.publisher: NIS Cooperation Group work stream on PQC
provenance.excerpt: 2. By 31.12.2030: • The Next Steps have been implemented by all Member States. • The PQC transition for high-risk use cases has been completed.
provenance.locator: Section 4.1, Timeline for the transition to PQC, p. 7

provenance.title: A Coordinated Implementation Roadmap for the Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography, Part 1, Version 1.1 (11.06.2025)
provenance.publisher: NIS Cooperation Group work stream on PQC
provenance.excerpt: At the same time, high-risk use cases should be transitioned to PQC as soon as possible, no later than the end of 2030.

provenance.title: A Coordinated Implementation Roadmap for the Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography
provenance.excerpt: The EU Member States, supported by the Commission, issued a roadmap and timeline to start using a more complex form of cybersecurity, the so-called post-quantum cryptography (PQC).

deadlines.label: EU roadmap: move completed for medium-risk use cases, and for low-risk use cases as far as feasible

provenance.title: A Coordinated Implementation Roadmap for the Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography, Part 1, Version 1.1 (11.06.2025)
provenance.publisher: NIS Cooperation Group work stream on PQC
provenance.excerpt: 3. By 31.12.2035: • The PQC transition for medium-risk use cases has been completed. • The PQC transition for low-risk use cases has been completed as much as feasible.
provenance.locator: Section 4.1, Timeline for the transition to PQC, p. 7

provenance.title: A Coordinated Implementation Roadmap for the Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography, Part 1, Version 1.1 (11.06.2025)
provenance.publisher: NIS Cooperation Group work stream on PQC
provenance.excerpt: By 2035, the transition should be completed for as many systems as practically feasible.

provenance.title: A Coordinated Implementation Roadmap for the Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography
provenance.excerpt: The EU Member States, supported by the Commission, issued a roadmap and timeline to start using a more complex form of cybersecurity, the so-called post-quantum cryptography (PQC).
